question: Read Figure 5.8. Which two regions are highlighted as having low female labor force participation?

Figure 5.7
Bar chart titled 'There is a substantial gap between low- and high-income countries in female educational attainment'. Vertical axis: 'Share of women age 25+ with at least upper-secondary education (%)', scaled from 0 to 80. Four orange bars with value labels: LICs 6.4; LMICs 27.0; UMICs 52.5; HICs 69.3. Source shown: 'WDR 2024 team.' Note states the figure illustrates educational attainment of women 25+ years of age for at least upper-secondary education; data cover 141 countries; HICs = high-income countries, LICs = low-income countries, LMICs = lower-middle-income countries, UMICs = upper-middle-income countries.

Figure 5.12
Scatter plot titled 'Women lag behind men in having financial accounts'. X-axis: 'GDP per capita (constant PPP 2017 US$1,000, log scale)' with visible tick labels around 50 and 100. Y-axis: 'Account ownership gap (percentage points)' with tick marks from about -10 to 40. The plotted points show the absolute difference in financial account ownership between men and women across 157 countries. A dark downward-sloping trend line runs roughly from about 6-7 percentage points at low GDP per capita to about 1-2 points at the highest GDP per capita, with a dotted horizontal zero line across the plot. Several countries are labeled in orange on the scatter: Morocco (around 24-25), Nigeria (around 17-18), Bangladesh (around 12-13), China (around 6-7), Colombia (around 9-10), Chile (around 5-6), and Sweden (around 0 or slightly below). Many unlabeled light-blue points are scattered throughout, with some higher-gap outliers near 20-35 percentage points and several points near zero or slightly negative. Sources noted below the plot: Global Findex (Global Financial Inclusion Database), World Bank, Washington, DC, https://globalfindex.worldbank.org/#data_sec_focus; WDI (World Development Indicators) (DataBank), World Bank, Washington, DC, https://databank.worldbank.org/source/world-development-indicators. Note states the figure shows the absolute difference (in percentage points) in 157 countries between the share of men with a financial account and the share of women with a financial account; accounts include those in financial institutions and mobile accounts. GDP = gross domestic product; PPP = purchasing power parity.

Figure 5.12
Scatter plot titled 'Women lag behind men in having financial accounts'. X-axis: 'GDP per capita (constant PPP 2017 US$1,000, log scale)' with visible tick labels around 50 and 100. Y-axis: 'Account ownership gap (percentage points)' with tick marks from about -10 to 40. The plotted points show the absolute difference in financial account ownership between men and women across 157 countries. A dark downward-sloping trend line runs roughly from about 6-7 percentage points at low GDP per capita to about 1-2 points at the highest GDP per capita, with a dotted horizontal zero line across the plot. Several countries are labeled in orange on the scatter: Morocco (around 24-25), Nigeria (around 17-18), Bangladesh (around 12-13), China (around 6-7), Colombia (around 9-10), Chile (around 5-6), and Sweden (around 0 or slightly below). Many unlabeled light-blue points are scattered throughout, with some higher-gap outliers near 20-35 percentage points and several points near zero or slightly negative. Sources noted below the plot: Global Findex (Global Financial Inclusion Database), World Bank, Washington, DC, https://globalfindex.worldbank.org/#data_sec_focus; WDI (World Development Indicators) (DataBank), World Bank, Washington, DC, https://databank.worldbank.org/source/world-development-indicators. Note states the figure shows the absolute difference (in percentage points) in 157 countries between the share of men with a financial account and the share of women with a financial account; accounts include those in financial institutions and mobile accounts. GDP = gross domestic product; PPP = purchasing power parity.
